fact.quote: (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, no property shall be exempted from ad valorem taxation unless the exemption is approved by two-thirds of the members elected to each branch of the General Assembly in a roll-call vote and by a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon.
fact.why: Kind: a statewide referendum on a general Act (HB 820, enacted as Act 346 per the legislature's annual summary: 'Effective May 3, 2018, and subject to a statewide referendum.'), held 'on November 6, 2018'. II(a)(1) of the Georgia Constitution, and that paragraph (legislature's annotated Constitution, 2016 edition, quoted) requires approval by two-thirds of each house and 'a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon'. The Act's own Section 3 says the same in votes cast: 'If more than one-half of the votes cast on such question are for approval of the Act' (the sentence runs on to the next numbered line, so only the single-line part is quoted in the act field). Share needed = more than one-half of the votes cast on the question = 0.5. Caveats: the text saved is the Senate Finance substitute, not the final enrolled Act (the legislature's summary of Act 346 describes the same 'municipal purposes' exemption); the Constitution text is the 2016 edition.

2024-measure-GA-STATEWIDE_REFERENDUM_QUE.type_quote: Do you approve the Act that increases an exemption from property tax for all tangible personal property from $7,500 to $20,000?

fact.quote: (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, no property shall be exempted from ad valorem taxation unless the exemption is approved by two-thirds of the members elected to each branch of the General Assembly in a roll-call vote and by a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon.
fact.why: Kind: a statewide referendum on a general Act (HB 808, enacted as Act 581 per the legislature's annual summary), raising the tangible personal property exemption from $7,500 to $20,000; the legislature's own brief says it 'must now be approved by Georgia voters during the November 5, 2024 general election'. HB 808 Section 2 cites Art. VII, Sec. II, Para. II(a)(1), which (legislature's annotated Constitution, quoted) needs two-thirds of each house and 'a majority of the qualified electors of the state voting in a referendum thereon'; HB 808 Section 3 says 'If more than one-half of the votes cast on such question are for approval of the Act' (sentence runs to the next numbered line, so only the single-line part is quoted in the act field). Share needed = more than one-half of the votes cast = 0.5. Caveats: the Constitution text is the 2016 edition (the SOS's current edition could not be read); the saved HB 808 text is the House Ways and Means substitute (LC 50 0782S), not the final Act 581, and the legislature's summary of Act 581 also says 'Subject to the timely ratification of a constitutional amendment', which the substitute does not contain, so the final text may differ; the ballot question quoted is the same in the brief and the substitute.
